clue.text: Pad in the saddle, with case attached

parts.note: a rider in the saddle is up on the horse
a holster is the leather case for a pistol

explanation.surface: A rider fits padding to the saddle and hangs a gun case from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' looks like a noun for the saddle, but it is a verb meaning to stuff furniture with padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad a chair or sofa with stuffing and cover it is the verb's main sense.

clue.text: Characteristic of a duckling in America, beginning to get crow's-feet

indicators.note: the US letters wrap around the next pieces, which sit in America
only the opening letter of the word get is taken

parts.note: crow's-feet are the wrinkles or lines at the corners of the eyes

explanation.surface: An American watches a young duck and starts to notice wrinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: The duckling is Hans Christian Andersen's Ugly Duckling, whose defining trait gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugly duckling of the fairy tale is known chiefly for its plain, unattractive looks.

clue.text: Peasant and I both used this language

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer or peasant

explanation.surface: A peasant and the speaker both spoke the same tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: HIND is a Scottish and northern English farm worker; the language is the main one of northern India.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is a principal language of India, so it is one example of a language.

clue.text: Criminal needs to arrange counsel, a barrister, ultimately

indicators.note: the letters are to be arranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the final letter of barrister is taken

explanation.surface: A criminal must line up a lawyer, and in the end a barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrange' rearranges COUNSEL, A and R (the last letter of 'barrister').
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so a larcenous act or person is thieving and criminal.

clue.text: Function changed in the middle, moved into marquee

indicators.note: the middle piece is moved inside the tent, as into a marquee

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent

indicators.note: only the central letters of changed are kept, its first two and last dropped

explanation.surface: A gathering is reorganised halfway through and shifted into a big tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' takes ANGE from inside 'changed' (losing C, H and D); 'moved into' puts it inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tangent is one of the trigonometric functions, alongside sine and cosine.

clue.text: Book about tennis action

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
a serve is the stroke that starts each point in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone reads a book about how to serve at tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a noun but is the verb, to book a table.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve a seat or room is to book it in advance, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Pair in trouble for days on end

clue.text: A Liberal member exhibiting uneasiness

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician shows signs of nervousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is anxiety or fear, a stronger form of uneasiness.

clue.text: In former capital perform Latvian opera

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed in the former capital

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro was the capital of Brazil until 1960
to go is to perform or act, as in having a go
a Lett is a Latvian

explanation.surface: Someone stages a Latvian opera in an old capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Brasilia replaced Rio as Brazil's capital, hence 'former capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's opera about a hunchbacked court jester, so it is one example of an opera.

clue.text: Copper going into case of missing insect

indicators.note: the copper symbol goes into the word for missing, which acts as its case

parts.note: something missing is lost
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman goes into a box where a missing insect was kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal; 'case of' only says LOST is the casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A locust is a large grasshopper that swarms and strips crops, so it is an insect.

clue.text: Vessel right on course

indicators.note: in an across clue, the right letter is placed on, after, the word for course

parts.note: a line is a course or route

explanation.surface: A ship keeps to the correct heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Thus clings to a recollection?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Thus clings to a recollection?' (9): CLINGS TO A rearranges to the answer, but the clue as held has no anagram indicator ('Thus' cannot serve) and the scan is unreadable

clue.text: Back in France, and spa shows a lack of sophistication

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: et is French for and
Evian is a French spa town known for its water

explanation.surface: Someone back from a French spa town shows how unworldly they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns ET plus EVIAN, giving TE and NAIVE in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence or simplicity, the opposite of worldly sophistication.

clue.text: Fratricide from Zulus — heads will roll

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words roll away and are lost

explanation.surface: Zulu warriors threaten that people will be killed for a brother's murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads will roll' drops F and Z, the first letters of 'from Zulus'. Romulus killed his twin brother Remus at the founding of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A fratricide is a person who kills a brother, as Romulus killed Remus.

clue.text: Preserve terrestrial elite

parts.note: to salt meat or fish is to preserve it
terrestrial means belonging to the world or ground

explanation.surface: A call to protect the finest people on the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the best and worthiest people, a moral elite.

clue.text: Completely blameless, I tell why I should be freed

indicators.note: the letters are freed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An innocent prisoner explains why they should be released.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a defendant's plea; 'should be freed' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily-white means pure and spotless, so without any blame.

clue.text: Located an assembly of short stories

indicators.note: the letters are assembled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gathering of short tales has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short tale, so anecdotal evidence or writing consists of them.

clue.text: Points company put in bulletin

parts.note: the compass points north, east, west, south give N, E, W, S
the cast is the company of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A theatre company is mentioned in a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: A newscast is a broadcast news bulletin on radio or television.

clue.text: Doctor chose one bottle, blue

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or alter it

explanation.surface: A physician picks a bottle and feels gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' reads as sad, but here it means risque; a joke close to the bone is near the knuckle.
explanation.definitionFit: Humour that is close to the bone is near indecency, which is what blue means of jokes.

clue.text: Supreme leader, covered by."Excessively good man"

indicators.note: the leader is enclosed by the word for excessively

parts.note: too means excessively
PM, Prime Minister, is the national leader
St, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A leader is praised by a sceptic as a little too virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Topmost means highest of all, so supreme in position.

clue.text: Tart with crust containing bread

indicators.note: the crust holds the bread inside it

parts.note: the crust is the top of a pie
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A pastry tart with a crust over a bread filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like the pastry, but it is the slang for a loose woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old disparaging words for a promiscuous woman.

clue.text: What a sauce — after leader is placed second, behaves badly

indicators.note: the leading letter of the sauce is moved to second place

parts.note: catsup is an American spelling of ketchup, a sauce

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a sauce and then misbehaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after leader is placed second' moves the C of CATSUP behind the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is a phrasal verb for misbehaving or playing up.

clue.text: Female undergarment — bloomers cover this

parts.note: a cow is the female of cattle and other animals
a slip is a woman's undergarment

explanation.surface: A woman's underwear, with bloomers worn over it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers seem to be knickers, but they are flowering plants, a heading that covers this wild flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow spring wild flower, one of the plants that bloom.

clue.text: Thread lost at first by Man?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of lost is taken

parts.note: the Isle of Man, so Man is one example of an isle

explanation.surface: A thread goes missing early on, taken by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, the island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread used for stockings.

clue.text: Complex man turned up inside one's dictionary first

indicators.note: the dictionary abbreviation goes first in the answer

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the word for one's

parts.note: one's means one is, giving I and S

indicators.note: the word up is turned around

explanation.surface: A man with a complex turns up within the pages of his dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Freud named the Oedipus complex after the king of Greek myth who unknowingly married his mother; 'first' is the charade's order signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus gave his name to Freud's Oedipus complex, so he is the man behind a complex.

clue.text: Careered into lodger, a nasty collision

indicators.note: the word for careered goes into the abbreviation for lodger

parts.note: PG, paying guest, is a lodger
to career is to run headlong, so careered gives ran

explanation.surface: Someone speeding crashes into their lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a crash, especially in a car or plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A prang is a slang word for a crash, so a collision.

clue.text: Continental accompaniment to rock cake

parts.note: Swiss is one nationality on the European continent
roll goes with rock in rock and roll

explanation.surface: A European musical partner for a rock cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock cake' reads as one bun, but rock belongs to the wordplay and only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a thin sponge cake spread with jam and rolled up.

clue.text: It's about a man who paints headgear

indicators.note: the word it is turned about

parts.note: the word it, with the 's as a link
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A painter's work centres on a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: An RA is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London, a standard crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headdress, a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Member of the Corvidae, extremely corvine — rook, perhaps

parts.note: pie is an old name for the magpie, one of the crow family

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of corvine are taken

explanation.surface: A rook is described as a typical crow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the rook a bird of the crow family; here it is a chess piece, also called a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the rook is one of the pieces, so it is an example of a piece.

clue.text: This could afford access to penthouse of the highest quality

definitions.text: This could afford access to penthouse
definitions.meaning: the uppermost staircase in a building leads to the apartment at the top

explanation.surface: A staircase to the penthouse is described as first-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means first-rate, while the top flight of stairs reaches the highest storey.
